note: Claude Opus 5.5 subagent, effort max, fresh session; kit copy without calibration/ or CHANGELOG

findings.title: Around DST changes the .at(time, tz) next-run arithmetic is off by the offset change: a job set inside the spring-forward gap runs twice the next day, and one rescheduled in the hour before its time after a fall-back skips a day
every(0) or a negative interval never returns: .do() spins forever in _schedule_next_run
Job argument values (credentials too, if passed) are written to the DEBUG log on every run
A job that raises is never rescheduled: it re-runs on every later run_pending() call and starves the other due jobs
Calling .do() twice on one Job registers it twice, so it runs twice per tick
On a fall-back night, a job in another time zone than the machine's, whose next run lands in the repeated local hour, runs on every run_pending() call for up to an hour
No clock seam: the library calls datetime.datetime.now() directly in nine places, so tests must swap out the global datetime class
Job writes into its Scheduler's list, and the module exposes the default scheduler's internal list as schedule.jobs
The package ships py.typed, but the fluent builder is untyped: after every(), the chain is Any to type-checking users
Contracts are loose: time units and weekdays are bare strings checked late, and at()'s tz annotation (Optional[str]) hides that it also takes pytz objects
Time-zone support is hard-wired to pytz: stdlib zoneinfo zones are refused, and supporting them means changing at() and the offset-correction code
Packaging metadata is declared twice, in setup.py and pyproject.toml, and the copies already disagree
Small inconsistencies: typos in user-facing messages and three string-formatting styles side by side
Job.at is the complexity hotspot: cyclomatic complexity 25 over 89 lines mixing zone lookup, per-unit format checks and parsing
Seven copy-pasted weekday properties (76 lines) differ only in the day name
The time-zone next-run code is a churn-and-complexity hotspot: reworked by each of the last three logic changes, and still wrong around DST changes
DST tests compute one reschedule from hand-picked times instead of replaying runs at the scheduled times, so the double run after a DST change passes
Failure and misuse paths are untested: no job raises, no zero or negative interval, and last_run is never asserted
until() tests mock 1 January, which hides the month and day handling of time-only deadlines
Some error messages mislead: a literal '{}' instead of the hour, an inverted 'latest is greater than interval', and an hourly format hint that contradicts the docstring
Inputs of the wrong kind fail with Python-internal errors that don't say what to do: aware datetimes in until(), a string interval, a missing pytz
The README quickstart fails as written: 'pip install schedule' doesn't install pytz, and the example's time-zone line needs it
The usage guide misstates when every(5).hours.at('20:30') first runs: 06:20:30 in the docs, 07:20:30 in practice
The API reference leaves out repeat() and every exception class, and its 'Exceptions' section lists only CancelJob, which is not an exception
Small factual slips: the fall-back DST example describes the clock moving forward, an until() example uses a 2020 deadline that always raises, and the README says 'Tested on Python and 3.7'
The documented dev workflow fails: requirements-dev.txt doesn't install on Python 3.13, and where it does, the documented test command (and any pytest run) crashes at startup
No contribution guide or agent instructions: nothing says how to lint, type-check or run one test, or what the conventions are
Releases are manual and the documented steps don't work as written: the version is bumped by hand in two files, 'python3 -m build' needs a package the docs never install, and only a wheel is built
CI has no lint gate: nothing runs flake8, ruff or pylint, so unused imports and similar slips reach master
repr() of a job that has no unit yet raises TypeError, so inspecting a half-built job in a REPL or log crashes
run_all(delay_seconds) also sleeps after the last job, so it always takes one delay longer than needed
The package claims 'OS Independent', but CI runs only on Linux and the test suite cannot run on Windows (time.tzset at import)
The build relies on a setuptools feature with an announced end date (license as a TOML table) while the build requirement is unbounded
No automated dependency updates, and the dev toolchain's only pin is six years stale: black 20.8b1 (4 advisories) kept alive by a click pin, with CI actions on old majors
Patch release 1.2.2 removed Job.period, a public attribute listed in the 1.2.1 API reference, without a deprecation or a changelog note
No deprecation mechanism and an implicit public surface: no DeprecationWarning anywhere, no __all__, and every working attribute of Job is public
No thread-safety contract: the docs run the scheduler in a background thread but never say which calls are safe from other threads, and nothing is locked
